_notes: bazel_args: the aquery invocation this migration is compared against.
exclude_targets: the three loadable-extension targets are out of scope for this migration (a loadable .dylib per extension is not built by //...), so neither side contributes their TUs.
ignore.defines NS_BLOCK_ASSERTIONS=1, _FORTIFY_SOURCE=1: injected by Bazel's macOS toolchain in opt mode; no CMake counterpart.

ignore.defines DUCKDB_SOURCE_ID, DUCKDB_VERSION, EXT_VERSION_CORE_FUNCTIONS, EXT_VERSION_PARQUET, DUCKDB_EXTENSION_DIRECTORIES: their values contain quote characters. CMake execs the compiler directly and passes the quotes through; Bazel runs it through a shell, so BUILD.bazel backslash-escapes them. The compiler receives the same macro value either way (verified by building those TUs), but the argv token is spelled differently.
ignore.link_flags -DNDEBUG, -Wthread-safety: CMake repeats the compile flags on the link line; Bazel does not.

include_map third_party/pcg -> @pcq: CMake passes third_party/pcg, a directory that does not exist in the tree (the directory is third_party/pcq). Bazel validates include roots, so it can only be spelled correctly there.
include_map codegen: the configure_file() output directory, spelled bazel-build/codegen/include under CMake and codegen/ under Bazel.

source_map generated_extension_loader.cpp: the configure_file() output, spelled bazel-build/codegen/src/... under CMake and at the exec-config root under Bazel. The 'bazel-out' prefix covers the config segment of the Bazel path; it is the only generated TU in the build.
target_map: Bazel target keys are full labels, so each CMake executable name maps to its ':name' Bazel label.

exclude_targets debug_fs_loadable_extension: its three sources are also compiled by test_debug_fs_extension with different defines (the loadable build sets DUCKDB_BUILD_LOADABLE_EXTENSION and drops the *_LINKED pair). Excluding the duplicate leaves one producer per source on both sides, so the TU has an unambiguous representative.

ignore.defines DUCKDB_ROOT_DIRECTORY, DUCKDB_BUILD_DIRECTORY: CMake bakes this checkout's absolute paths in; Bazel has no compile-time source root. BUILD.bazel substitutes '.' (the runfiles tree under `bazel test`, where the declared data lives) for the root directory.

tests: CMake's File API carries no role for test targets, so DuckDB's ~30 test object libraries and the unittest binary classify as production and are diffed through the normal library/executable stages -- include_tests stays false because a role-based test phase would compare two empty sets.

test sharding: one cc_test per second-level test directory, split in two because `-f` clears the whole Catch2 registry (test/unittest.cpp) and registers only the listed corpus files: unittest_<slug>_test = `-f <its .test>`, unittest_<slug>_slow_test = `-f <its .test_slow>`, unittest_<slug>_cpp_test = `~*.test ...`, unittest_<slug>_cpp_slow_test = `[.] ~*.test ...`. The shards cover the whole suite (verified 7321/7321 cases, none in no shard). test/extension's one TEST_CASE gets a target of its own because it binds a fixed socket, which would collide if it ran in every shard.

fixture trees: a corpus file that globs `dir/**` cannot see through the runfiles symlink farm (LocalFileSystem::CrawlDirectoryLevel skips symlinks), so a shard containing one gets a real copy of data/ from the fixture_tree rule in duckdb_codegen.bzl. Every shard ships the whole test/, data/ and third_party/ trees, because tests read fixtures from other directories by path (a .test_template in test/sql/tpch, the CSVs under test/sakila/data).

known difference: test/sql/copy/csv/glob/read_csv_glob_crawl.test_slow:6 asserts that the current working directory holds files (`count(*) > 0 from glob('**')`). CMake runs the suite from the project source root; Bazel runs it from a runfiles tree where every file is a symlink, so a `**` crawl matches nothing. That test's `**/samename/*` crawl and the crawl/partition tests beside it pass, because they start inside a path prefix instead of at the working directory.
